I'll simply have to disagree here. Private property is not having exclusive rights to an object. It is having exclusive rights to an object you could never personally make use of. For example, a factory, or hundreds of acres of land. Personal property is the term for items you have exclusive rights to because you are or can in the near future make personal use of it. For example, your house, car, computer, etc. Items your labor produces would also be considered personal property, at least temporarily, and this is what would be traded in a mutualist economy. Goods produced would become your personal property to do what you choose with, and then you can trade these for other things you need or want.
